answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each agent identity holds a score that decays exponentially: every interaction with a counterparty older than a set window applies a per-identity audit fee drawn from its score. Fresh clones start at baseline and face a steeper decay gradient, like a nebula thinning at its edge. To keep ten clones viable through a tundra of low activity, an attacker pays recurring scoring refreshes. Crossing the canyon from baseline to trusted requires sustained paid interactions, so mass identity creation costs scale superlinearly with clone count.
